dohori.note: Commercial lok dohori, the recorded male-female duet that grew out of the Gurung rodhi ghar and the dohori sanjh restaurants: Prem Raja Mahat's Music Nepal duets of the 1990s, the Indreni Cassette Centre lok dohori releases of 2008-2011, Bishnu Majhi's hits with Yam Chhetri, Pashupati Sharma and Kulendra Bishwakarma, Prakash Saput's 'Dohori Battle' and 'Bola Maya', and the live studio dohori sessions of the 2020s. Field recordings of improvised village dohori are missing: none could be found on a page a script can read.

tamangselo.note: Opens with Kunti Moktan's pop-selo hit, Kutumba's instrumental, the genre's pioneer Hira Devi Waiba (HMV) and a 1996 cassette selo. The peak runs from instrumental tunes named Tamang Selo (sarangi, flute, folk bands) through the 2009-2010 Indreni cassette albums sung in Tamang to current singles. Most ties are by title: the track, or the album it is on, names the genre; Hira Devi Waiba, Navneet Aditya Waiba and Indira Gole Gurung are tied through their performer pages, Kunti Moktan through the Kathmandu Post.

pasillo.note: Covers both national branches. Ecuador: the Dúo Ecuador's 1930s records, Carlota Jaramillo 'La Reina del Pasillo', the Dúo Benítez-Valencia, Julio Jaramillo and Olimpo Cárdenas, the Hermanos Miño Naranjo (whose 'Tú y yo' won in Barcelona) and the modern revival of Juan Fernando Velasco and the Museo del Pasillo. Colombia: Jorge Villamil and José A. Morales pasillos sung by Garzón y Collazos and Silva y Villalba, and the instrumental pasillos of Fulgencio García and Luis A. Calvo played by Oriol Rangel. Release years are those on the store pages, mostly compilations and reissues, not first recordings; the Venezuelan vals and Central American pasillo are not represented.

meringue.note: Built around the 1940s-50s Port-au-Prince dance orchestras, above all Issa El-Saieh's La Belle Créole 78s, whose labels and discography mark each side 'Meringue' (with Guy Durosier, Wébert Sicot and Bebo Valdés's Haitian sessions), and around the salon méringue for piano: Fabre Duroseau's 1952 Folkways recordings and Ludovic Lamothe playing his own 'Nibo' for Lomax in 1937. Péligre is a carnival méringue of 1955. The Lomax tracks were recorded 1936-37 and first issued in 2009; the Destiné track is from 1952-62 and first issued in 2015. Saintonge's Élégie-Méringue and Casséus's Méringue Frangeul are modern recordings of art pieces. Choucoune ('Ti zwazo', 1893) is the best-known méringue of all.

gaitazuliana.note: Built on the classic Maracaibo conjuntos of the 1960s-80s: Ricardo Aguirre 'El Monumental' (with Cardenales del Éxito and Saladillo), the Cardenales, Estrellas del Zulia, early Guaco, Gran Coquivacoa's tamborera, Rincón Morales, Maracaibo 15 and Barrio Obrero's protest gaita 'Un ojo dimos'. Most tracks come from Discomoda and Foca compilations or digital reissues; years are the dates those pages give, null where only a compilation date was read.

pasodoble.note: Two halves of one form. The band pasodoble: the taurino, militar and festero classics (La Gracia de Dios 1880 to Ragón Falez 1935) in modern recordings by the Banda Sinfónica Municipal de Madrid, the Las Ventas bullring band, La Artística de Buñol and the Villena band for Moros y Cristianos. The sung pasodoble canción: Raquel Meller, Concha Piquer, Estrellita Castro, Celia Gámez, Juanita Reina, Joselito, Lolita Sevilla, Manolo Escobar, Marifé de Triana and Perlita de Huelva. The band recordings are from 1995-2020, not period recordings; no 1920s band 78 was found on a readable page. Ballroom (DanceSport) pasodoble and the Mexican, Puerto Rican and Ecuadorian pasodobles are left out.

albums: The Art of Harana: Serenades for Guitar
harana.note: Built on two voices: Ruben Tagalog, the crooner of the radio show Harana ni Ruben Tagalog, from a Villar Records collection whose original recording dates are not on any page read (years left null), and the Harana Kings, three old provincial haranistas recorded with guitarist Florante Aguilar in 2012, singing Tagalog and Ilocano serenades (Dardarepdep, No Duaduaem Pay). Florante Aguilar's three tracks are solo-guitar versions of serenade songs, including the Cebuano Usahay and Matud Nila; Charmaine Clamor's Harana sa Dilim is a jazz singer's modern take.

jiangnansizhu.note: The repertoire is small, so pieces recur on purpose: the Eight Great Pieces (三六, 欢乐歌, 行街, 中花六板/薰风曲, 慢六板, 四合如意, 云庆, 花三六/慢三六) heard from different ensembles. Built around the Lu Chunling, Zhou Hui, Zhou Hao and Ma Shenglong quartet (1983 China Record cassette), Shanghai conservatory and club groups (上海音乐学院教授丝竹研究组, 上海国乐研究社, Shanghai Traditional Music Society), a Shanghai teahouse ensemble, the Shanghai Chinese Orchestra's 1991 set of the eight pieces, and later readings (Guo Gan and Lingling Yu 2011, 华韵乐府 2015, 范临风 2024). 梵王宫 is another name of 阳八曲, and 薰风曲 of 中花六板. Release years are those of the edition read; the Naxos tracks carry 1992-93 dates and the 2002 Naxos ℗.
